name: Abimelech
overview: Abimelech was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, known uniquely as the son of Gideon (also called Jerubbaal) by a concubine in Shechem. His life is marked by violent ambition, as he killed his seventy brothers to secure power. His death came when a woman dropped a millstone on him, mortally wounding him, after which his armor bearer killed him to preserve his honor.
namesAndTitles: The name Abimelech means '[my] father is king' or '[my] father is Molech,' reflecting a title of authority or connection to a deity. This proper name was not given by God but is recorded in Judges 8:31.
familyAndRelationships: Abimelech was explicitly identified as the son of Gideon. Additionally, Zebul is inferred to have been a chief under Abimelech's rule, indicating a leadership structure during his time.
scriptureSignificance: Abimelech's significance in Scripture lies in his ruthless quest for power, demonstrating the dangers of self-exaltation apart from God's will. His fratricide and violent death illustrate the consequences of sin and rebellion within Israel's history. His story serves as a sober warning about the destructive outcomes of ungodly ambition.
